what_happened: In job qfax (a disk-space guard), the user corrected Athena's second reading before work began. The reading planned to edit athena.toml, but the 10G minimum free disk is already a default in config.rs, so no config edit is needed. It kept a criterion to delete a closed job's target/, which commit 173d12e had already landed. It used the word 'operator', which the boundary scan bans in Athena's files. It also did not clearly require a free-space check before dispatch and before the checks, although a job's build can need about 16 GB and the disk filled on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-25. The user narrowed the reading on all four points.
cause: The reading stage works from the request text and incident history, not from the repo's current state. It does not see what has already landed (173d12e), which settings already have code defaults, or the boundary word list. Nothing cross-checks a reading's deliverables, criteria or wording against those before it is accepted, so the user has to catch each mismatch. Related readings keep making this kind of miss, as with the email rule in case gp4k.
prevention: Add a pre-acceptance check on every reading. (1) Scan the reading text with the same banned-word list the boundary test uses and send it back on a hit. (2) Test each deliverable and criterion against recent history on main, and flag any that matches an already-landed commit. (3) Flag any athena.toml edit for a setting that already has a default in config.rs, and any new config field, unless the request needs it. Show the reader the banned-word list and the relevant defaults so the first reading is right.
proposed_request: Make Athena check free disk space before it dispatches a job and again before it runs the checks, and stop the job with a clear message when free space is below the minimum. The minimum is 10G. It is a default in config.rs that applies when the setting is absent. Do not edit athena.toml, so the running Athena never meets an unknown field. A job's build can need about 16 GB, and the disk filled on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-25, so both checks matter. Do not add anything about deleting a closed job's target/, because commit 173d12e already did that. Use the words 'the user' and never 'operator' in any file Athena owns, because the boundary scan bans that word. Acceptance: (1) with free space below the minimum, a test shows dispatch refuses and the job is not started; (2) with free space below the minimum, a test shows the checks do not run and the job reports low disk instead of a failed check; (3) with enough free space, both stages proceed as before; (4) the minimum is read from the config default and a test shows it applies when the setting is absent; (5) athena.toml is unchanged and the boundary scan passes.
